testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes in air brake systems must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: During an engine fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn the engine off as soon as possible.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: During an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if possible. Instead, spray foam through the louvers or from under the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if you do not drain the tanks in an air brake system?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the system.
The vehicle carries too much fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil. If water builds up in the system, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: Which braking system does the brake pedal control?
questions.explanation: The service brake system lets you apply and release the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.explanation: The number and size of air storage tanks differ depending on the vehicle. There is no fixed number used in all air brake systems.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, which lane should you drive in?
questions.explanation: The right lanes are for slower-moving traffic. If a heavy load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration a good practice?

options.text: Yes, it is encouraged at slow speeds.
Yes, it is encouraged at all speeds.
No, it can damage the vehicle.
No, it may confuse other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually to avoid jerking the vehicle. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to your truck.

questions.question: How can you deal with blind spots?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only need to watch vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to monitor traffic around you. This helps you notice when vehicles move into your blind spots.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.explanation: When parking during the stop/start maneuver on the driving test, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block driveways or intersections.

questions.question: How can you reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress can lead to dangerous, aggressive driving. Playing calming music can help you relax and stay focused while driving.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles enter the lane you want.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is already in the lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is already in the lane you want.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers you did not see a chance to move out of your way or honk to alert you. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks require special care because:

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift during travel. Be extra careful when turning and on curves with this type of vehicle.

questions.question: An item that is 40 feet long placed on a flatbed trailer should be secured by at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. Always use a minimum of two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle, like at dawn or dusk, you can help other drivers by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights to low beam when visibility is low. If you have trouble seeing others, they likely have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and accept delays to avoid dangerous driving. Plan for extra time when you start your trip to reduce stress about arriving late.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: Do not swing too wide to the left when turning right. Keep your rear close to the curb. Leaving space on your right while turning right signals to others that you are turning left, so they may try to pass on your right.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop driving and sleep if you feel tired. Trying to fight tiredness is dangerous and causes many fatal crashes. Energy pills do not make you more alert. Once they wear off, you will be even more tired than before.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car:

options.text: The officer will tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected because the violation is on your personal license.
You should tell your employer within six months.
You must tell your employer within 30 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: Tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction in any vehicle. This rule does not include parking violations.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact, do not speed up to challenge them, and do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: If a vehicle is found to be over-length during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:

options.text: Trim the length of the load.
Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are secured tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are secured tightly.
questions.explanation: If the vehicle is oversize, confirm that all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly fastened and that you have all required permits.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Check the exhaust system for problems. Look for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, or stacks. Check for loose, broken, or missing brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts. Watch for exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other vehicle parts. Look for leaks in the exhaust system.

questions.question: A burning tire should be:
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use large amounts of water to fully cool the tire.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black from debris on the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin layer of clear ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet rather than icy.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce normal braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with your vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS activates during hard braking to prevent the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: While driving, look ahead to spot possible dangers. Plan how you will handle each danger if it becomes unsafe.

questions.question: A sign showing a maximum safe speed:

options.text: Is a suggestion only. Vehicles may travel faster than the posted speed.
Applies only to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
Must be followed. No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be followed. No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should check your tires to:

options.text: See if the tires are rolling properly.
See if the tread is sufficient.
Compare tire size to other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to spot tire fires. Tire fires can start when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch each other, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
Should not be on the roadway.
Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving with cargo, the driver should:

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
Ask other drivers about their cargo.
Use side mirrors only to check the cargo.
Skip checks if the cargo was secured before starting the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles of the trip.
questions.explanation: Check and secure cargo before starting a trip. After you start driving, stop and check the load within the first 50 miles. Check again every three hours or every 150 miles traveled, and after each stop.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk, when other vehicles cannot see you well, you can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: What color is the ABS malfunction lamp?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: In the basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to do which of these?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include: straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What blood alcohol content (BAC) is illegal when driving a commercial vehicle?
questions.explanation: Driving a commercial vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal. For a first offense, you will lose your license for at least one year. If your BAC is below 0.04 percent but alcohol is detected, you will be taken out of service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
To make the compressor run more efficiently.
To lubricate parts of the braking system.
To prevent rust from forming on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the braking system to keep ice from forming.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, how many points of contact must you maintain with the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. If your vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. If you exit incorrectly, you will automatically fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: It is safest to avoid driving in fog. If you must drive through fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.question: When checking your tires, which is NOT a problem to fix?

options.text: Radial and bias-ply tires used together
Tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch on the front tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch on the front tires
questions.explanation: When inspecting tires, check for: air pressure that is too low or too high; mixing radial and bias-ply tires; tread depth less than 4/32 of an inch in main grooves on front tires; and tread depth less than 2/32 of an inch on all other tires.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which do you NOT need to do?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the power steering fluid dipstick is and prove there is enough fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Complete the test with no accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: What should you do with your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Only use them when there is traffic.
Check them regularly, but only on cloudy days.

questions.explanation: Be aware of your surroundings at all times. Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: In work zones, follow the posted speed limits. Slow down if road or weather conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: Overloading cargo can harm all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Too much cargo can harm steering, braking, and speed control. Pay attention to how your vehicle handles when carrying extra weight.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: There is no trailer attached to the tractor.
The vehicle is on a slight incline.
The vehicle is on a slight decline.

questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a tractor, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, you should watch the road about ____ ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to spot dangers early. At highway speeds, you should watch about 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This is roughly a quarter mile.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Creates a loud squeaking noise when being used.
Helps to ensure control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps to ensure control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control while braking. It does not change how far it takes to stop.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of deaths and injuries in work zones. Drive carefully around road workers.

questions.question: The minimum size of placards identifying hazardous materials is:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: Skids caused by acceleration can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: To fix a skid caused by acceleration, take your foot off the accelerator. On very slippery surfaces, you may also need to push the clutch in.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Stop harder than you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What should be used to check tire pressure?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure during a vehicle inspection. Simply kicking the tires is not enough to pass.
